title: Collective Charge-\(2e\) Bosonic Excitations in Charge-Ordered Systems
abstract: Charge order is conventionally characterized by a static modulation of the electronic density, while its collective excitations remain less developed from a quasiparticle perspective than those of spin-ordered systems. Here, we formulate the collective excititations of charge order within an effective charge-pseudospin model, in which the charge-ordered ground state is represented by staggered pseudospin order. Quantizing fluctuations around this ordered state via a Holstein--Primakoff transformation, we reveal two branches of bosonic quasiparticles with degenerate, gapped dispersions that carry opposite quantized electric charges $\pm 2e$. We therefore term these charge-$2e$ bosons ``\textit{bichargons},'' closely paralleling the two magnon branches of a bipartite antiferromagnet that carry opposite spin angular momenta. We show that a temperature gradient drives the diffusion of thermally excited bichargons, generating a charge Seebeck response when the degeneracy between the oppositely charged branches is lifted by tuning the chemical potential away from the charge-neutrality point. In contrast, despite carrying finite electric charges, a thermal bichargon gas remains electrically insulating under a static electric field because bichargon quasiparticle number is not conserved. An ac electric field, however, can parametrically generate coherent pairs of oppositely charged bichargons that support a finite dc drift current in the presence of a bias electric field, offering a bosonic analogue of photoconductivity mediated by photoexcited electron--hole pairs in semiconductors. Our results establish bichargons as a new class of collective bosonic charge carriers in charge-ordered systems and extend the quasiparticle paradigm of magnons in spin-ordered systems to the charge sector, with electric charge replacing spin angular momentum as the transported quantity.
summary: This theoretical work introduces 'bichargons,' quantized collective bosonic excitations carrying $\pm 2e$ charge in charge-ordered systems. It establishes that these excitations can mediate a charge Seebeck effect under a temperature gradient, while also predicting a unique photoconductivity mechanism driven by AC fields. This extends the magnon concept to the charge sector, providing a new framework for understanding charge transport in correlated materials.
main_problem: To determine if staggered charge-pseudospin order can support collective quasiparticle excitations carrying electric charge, analogous to magnons in spin-ordered systems.
main_result: The theory predicts the existence of 'bichargons' ($\pm 2e$ bosons) that mediate a charge Seebeck effect and can support a DC current via AC field excitation, extending the magnon paradigm to the charge sector.
method: The analysis involves formulating an effective charge-pseudospin model, quantizing fluctuations via Holstein-Primakoff transformation, and diagonalizing the resulting bosonic Hamiltonian using Bogoliubov transformations.
model_or_system: The system is a charge-ordered material modeled by an effective pseudospin-1/2 Hamiltonian derived from the extended Hubbard model, analyzed around the charge-neutrality point.
key_observables: Bichargon branches ($\pm 2e$ charge), Seebeck coefficient, DC charge current under bias, and the transition from insulating (static E-field) to conducting (AC field) behavior.
important_parameters:
Chemical potential ($\mu$) tuning away from charge-neutrality, temperature gradient ($
abla T$), and applied electric fields (static $E$ vs. AC).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the charge-ordered ground state is represented by staggered pseudospin order, and the quasiparticle number of bichargons is not conserved.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically compares the two oppositely charged bichargon excitations to their magnon counterparts in an antiferromagnet. Figure 2 illustrates the bichargon Seebeck effect and the resulting charge accumulation.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the model and derives the two gapped bosonic branches (bichargons). It then analyzes the thermal response (Seebeck effect) and the limitations under static fields. Finally, it explores the non-equilibrium transport driven by AC fields, establishing the new bosonic charge carrier.
why_interesting: The concept of bichargons provides a direct, charge-based analogue to magnons, allowing the application of established spin-transport physics (like the Seebeck effect) to charge-ordered Mott insulators, which is highly relevant for understanding correlated electron transport.

(a) When thermally excited bichargons are unequally populated in the two branches, their diffusion under a temperature gradient generates a net charge current and opposite charge accumulation at the two sample edges, constituting the charge counterpart of the magnonic spin Seebeck effect in antiferromagnets. The two equivalent processes carry equal and opposite charge currents, resulting in a vanishing macroscopic current, whereas an applied dc bias lifts this cancellation and drives a net dc charge current carried by the parametrically generated bichargon pairs, analogous to photoconductivity in semiconductors mediated by photoexcited electron–hole pairs.
